items.title: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
items.summary: War in Sudan has led to the worst humanitarian crisis with more than 33 million people in need of assistance according to the WHO The US and 30 other Western states have warned of an "alarming deterioration" in food security in Sudan, urging the warring sides in the civil war to remove obstacles to humanitarian aid to prevent famine In a joint statement, the signatories said conflict was the main driver of Sudan's hunger crisis, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting food production "There is very little to survive on," Yusuf Roble, regional director for Islamic Relief East Africa, told BBC Newsday, describing how people returning to Omdurman were finding their homes destroyed or looted The war, which began in April 2023, has displaced 14 million people The statement , external was signed by EU states, the UK, Canada, Switzerland and Norway, as well as the US, where it was published by the state department on Monday after first appearing on the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations website It estimates that 19.5 million people or 41% of Sudan's…

items.title: Myanmar: Is the US undermining the EU's diplomatic blockade?
items.summary: With the US reopening talks with Myanmar's military-backed government, and several Southeast Asian countries restarting diplomatic contacts, the EU is facing uncomfortable questions about its own boycott of the junta The US government has begun a quiet reproachment with Myanmar 's military-backed government, holding two rounds of talks since September with State Department representative Michael Vance. American diplomats reportedly meet Myanmar officials in Naypyitaw and then in Tokyo earlier this month Washington wants to tackle online scam centers, secure the release of imprisoned American businessman Adam Castillo, and potentially gain access to Myanmar's rare-earth resources . The market for the valuable minerals is currently controlled by the US rival China Meanwhile, Southeast Asian governments are also increasingly questioning their policy of isolating Myanmar's military leadership. Multiple countries have already renewed direct diplomatic contacts The EU, however, continues to reject the legitimacy of the military junta in the war-torn country.

items.summary: Maputo October 27, AZERTAC/AIM “A double standard policy should be totally eliminated from international politics,” President Ilham Aliyev said in his speech at the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue. items.title: Mental health is emerging challenge for health professionals – health minister
items.summary: Maputo, Oct 26 (AIM) – The Mozambican health minister Health Ussene believes that mental health is an emerging challenge in the training of health professionals in the country, arguing that there is need to create psychosocial support mechanisms to prevent excessive stress, burnout, and the abandonment of studies. Speaking on Monday in Maputo at the opening of the 5th National Meeting on the Training of Health Professionals, the minister acknowledged that training in the health sector often takes place in complex environments with high academic and emotional demands, circumstances that warrant greater attention to the well-being of students. According to the minister, the support provided to trainees should contribute to their holistic development and enable the identification of risk factors that could jeopardize the continuation of their studies and their professional preparation.

items.title: Mozambique: Government forecasts record gold production of 1,809 kg in 2027
items.summary: According to estimates in the 2027 budget proposal, the Government points to a “significant recovery” in the extractive industry, supported by the recovery of the main export minerals “In the metallic minerals sector, gold stands out, with production potentially increasing by around 44%,” it states The Executive expects gold production to reach 1,809.2 kilograms in 2027, above the 1,255.4 kilograms projected for 2026 and surpassing the previous high recorded in 2023 The data indicate that gold production rose from 764.4 kilograms in 2021 to 1,263.8 kilograms in 2022 and 1,666.4 kilograms in 2023, before declining to 1,625.8 kilograms in 2024 and 1,349.3 kilograms in 2025 The expected increase in production should also translate into higher export revenues At current international gold prices, the 1,809.2 kilograms projected for 2027 represent a gross market value of over US$230 million (€200 million) at current prices, although the actual value of production will depend on movements in international prices and marketing conditions The projected recovery comes during a period marked…

items.title: Co-ordinated cattle raids kill at least 72 people in South Sudan
items.summary: Cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities in South Sudan At least 72 people have been killed during cattle raids in South Sudan's northern Warrap state, according to the regional government An unspecified number of cattle were taken and homes burnt during what was a "co-ordinated attack" on Monday involving two communities in Tonj North county, the state authorities said Such deadly violence is often part of a cycle of revenge attacks as cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities and are also important as young men need them as dowries to get married Clashes over territory are also common across the country as it prepares to hold its first election since its independence in 2011 - delayed because of a brutal civil war The clashes occurred near the border of Warrap and Unity states in the area of Akop Payam, with some members from Lou Ariik community said to have attacked those from Apuk Padoch community William Wol Mayom Bol, Warrap state's information minister, said they followed deadly violence last Friday that claimed eight lives The…
